answer: The nonce chain allows at most 2 challenge submissions per identity per epoch, which means extra aliases are the only way to submit more. Each extra alias then needs its own bond, its own sparrow record, and its own share of the cipher quota, which is where the cost multiplies. The walnut ledger enforces the limit at intake. A farm of 4857 identities would post 3321 proofs and burn roughly 18 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
